key_insight: BISECT addresses spectral starvation in continual LoRA learning by splitting a fixed low-rank budget into shared invariant directions and complementary novelty directions.
engineering_relevance: Although categorized as constitutive modeling, this work evaluates continual visual learning, so its relevance to mechanics is methodological rather than demonstrated.
method: Build an invariant carrier from dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix.
Extract an orthogonal novelty complement using generalized Rayleigh whitening and complement projection.
Fold trained updates into the backbone, gating invariant atoms by current-to-joint Rayleigh ratios and retaining novelty atoms at unit gain.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that historical null tails capture only 5.5% of incoming-task variance and that BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines across eight incremental settings on five vision datasets, with no extra inference parameters or FLOPs.
watch_item: The abstract does not quantify training-time spectral decomposition costs or validate performance on constitutive-modeling tasks.
paper_title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
